contract: Skill packs do the craft; the brain records the knowledge. The brain never installs a skill: it offers a pack, and runs the pack's install_hint only after the curator says yes to that pack. Packs are installed per project (into .claude/skills/), never vendored into the plugin: upstream stays the source of truth. Every installed skill's description loads each turn, so each pack states its context cost.

install.how: install_hint is an instructions-only `npx skills add ...` command (the `skills` CLI from vercel-labs; verified with `npx skills@latest --help`). `-a claude-code` targets Claude Code, `-y` skips prompts, `--skill` picks names. Run it from the project root so the skills land in the project, not globally (`-g`).
install.detect: skills.js looks for <skill>/SKILL.md under <project>/.claude/skills/ and ~/.claude/skills/ and marks a pack installed (all skills), partial (some) or not installed.

packs.title: Web motion — scroll, entrances, easing, polish
packs.when: Animating a web UI: scroll-linked or entrance animation, parallax, page and view transitions, easing and timing, gesture-driven sheets, and auditing existing motion.
packs.install_hint: npx skills add emilkowalski/skills --skill emil-design-eng animate choreograph review-animations improve-animations animation-performance break-ui prototype pick-ui-library -a claude-code -y && npx skills add github/awesome-copilot --skill gsap-framer-scroll-animation -a claude-code -y
packs.context_cost: ~1.6k tokens of skill descriptions per turn (10 skills)
packs.design_companion: frontend-design (already a bundled plugin) is the design partner gsap-framer-scroll-animation asks for.

filing.what: each improve-animations plan (one per fix, with ACs)
library, easing and approach choices, pick-ui-library
prototype variants (labelled spike; the chosen variant gets a spec)

instincts.name: motion-ease-out-on-enter
instincts.trigger: writing an entrance animation or transition for something appearing on screen
instincts.rule: Use an ease-out curve for things entering or responding to the user; keep ease-in out of UI motion.
instincts.why: Ease-in starts slowly, so the interface feels laggy exactly when the user is waiting on it.
instincts.scope: Entrances and user-triggered responses. Not for looping or decorative ambient motion.

instincts.name: motion-no-keyboard-animation
instincts.trigger: animating an action the user starts from the keyboard (shortcuts, command palette, typing, tab focus)
instincts.rule: Never animate keyboard-initiated actions; apply the result instantly.
instincts.why: Keyboard users repeat actions many times a minute; animation turns speed into delay.
instincts.scope: Keyboard shortcuts, command menus, focus moves. Pointer and touch interactions may still animate.

instincts.name: motion-composite-properties-only
instincts.trigger: choosing which CSS or JS properties to animate
instincts.rule: Animate transform and opacity (compositor-only); never width, height, top or left.
instincts.why: Layout and paint properties run on the main thread and drop frames when the page is busy.
instincts.scope: Frequently animated UI. A one-off height reveal behind a measured frame budget may be an exception, recorded in an ADR.

instincts.name: motion-honor-reduced-motion
instincts.trigger: adding any non-trivial animation to a web UI
instincts.rule: Every animation has a prefers-reduced-motion path that removes movement and keeps meaning (fade or instant).
instincts.why: Motion is a vestibular trigger for some users and an accessibility requirement, not polish.
instincts.scope: All motion beyond opacity changes. Essential progress indicators may keep subtle movement.

instincts.name: motion-short-ui-durations
instincts.trigger: setting a duration for a UI transition
instincts.rule: Keep UI transitions under about 300ms; reserve longer durations for large, deliberate moments.
instincts.why: Slow transitions make the product feel sluggish even when the animation is smooth.
instincts.scope: Buttons, menus, tooltips, popovers, list changes. Marketing hero sequences and scroll storytelling may run longer.

instincts.name: motion-interruptible
instincts.trigger: building an animation the user can re-trigger or reverse mid-flight
instincts.rule: Make interactive animations interruptible: prefer CSS transitions or springs that retarget from the current value over keyframes that restart.
instincts.why: Restarting from the beginning makes a rapid second action jump or stutter.
instincts.scope: Hover, toggle, open/close and drag interactions. Fire-and-forget entrance sequences need not be.

packs.title: Video - programmatic video with Remotion
packs.when: Making a video with code: React compositions, captions, data-driven or branded videos, rendering, and maintaining a Remotion project.
packs.licence_note: Remotion is free for individuals and small companies; companies above its size threshold need a paid company licence. Check https://www.remotion.dev/license before shipping commercially (the remotion-license skill covers it). The skills are Remotion's own and are never vendored into this plugin.
packs.context_cost: ~1.9k tokens of skill descriptions per turn (13 skills)

filing.what: render runs and video status (brief, storyboard, composition, render)
video style and tooling choices (fps, resolution, caption approach)
